title: Electromagnetism
standard_text: The magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor and the right-hand rule; magnetic flux, Φ = BA cos θ; Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, ε = −NΔΦ/Δt; Lenz's law; applications of induction. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 11, Physics: Electromagnetism)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): fields around currents, magnetic flux, Faraday's law, Lenz's law and applications of induction. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A changing magnetic flux induces an emf.
body_html:
How to think about it

A current in a conductor produces a magnetic field around it; the right-hand rule gives its direction. Magnetic flux Φ = BA cos θ measures the field passing through an area.

Faraday's law: the induced emf is equal to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage, ε = −NΔΦ/Δt. Lenz's law (the minus sign): the induced current opposes the change that caused it. Induction is used in generators, transformers and induction stoves.

Example

Flux changes by 0,02 Wb in 0,1 s in a 100-turn coil. emf?

NΔΦ/Δt

Answer: 20 V

Example

A magnet is held still inside a coil. Is an emf induced?

Is the flux changing?

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a still magnet induces a current.
  • Forgetting the number of turns N.
  • Thinking Lenz's law means the current helps the change.

faq.q: How can you increase the induced emf?
faq.a: Move the magnet faster, use a stronger magnet or use more turns on the coil.

faq.q: Why does Lenz's law agree with conservation of energy?
faq.a: Work must be done against the opposing force, and this work becomes electrical energy.
